author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Veterinarian directory can be narrowed to one specialty by address
summary: Both forms of the veterinarian directory, the paged page and the machine-readable list, accept an optional specialty in the address and list only veterinarians holding it. The name matches as a whole, ignoring case. The machine-readable list is reinstated as a supported form (REQ-VET-004).
acceptance_criteria: [REQ-VET-003] given a specialty some veterinarians hold, when either form is requested for it, then only the veterinarians holding it are listed.
[REQ-VET-003] given a specialty name differing from the stored name only by letter case, when either form is requested for it, then it matches.
[REQ-VET-003] given only the opening part of a specialty name, when either form is requested for it, then no veterinarian matches.

[REQ-VET-003] given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when either form is requested for it, then the usual page or document is returned with an empty list, not an error (HTTP 200 per the owner's request).
[REQ-VET-003] given an empty or all-space specialty, when either form is requested, then the result matches a request naming no specialty.
[REQ-VET-003] given a narrowed list longer than one page, when the reader follows any page link, then the next page keeps the specialty and paging counts only the narrowed list.
[REQ-VET-004] given the clinic's veterinarians, when the machine-readable list is requested, then every veterinarian is returned with their specialties.
[REQ-VET-001] given no specialty, the directory page still lists every veterinarian a page at a time, unchanged.
Edge case 2: a name that is no specialty at all yields an empty list, not an error.
Edge case 3: a veterinarian holding several specialties appears once in a narrowed list and still shows every specialty they hold.
non_goals: No form, dropdown, or other page control for choosing a specialty on either surface (owner: 'The filter is a URL contract only'); a visible control may come as a follow-up request.
No pagination of the machine-readable list.
No behavior committed for a padded specialty name (spaces around a real name) or a repeated specialty parameter; both are recorded Open Questions. Tests must not lock either behavior.
No indication on the page of which specialty is active.
notes: Autofix audit: no prd-autofix records on the log; skipped. REQ ids: the owner asked for a fresh requirement for the reinstated JSON endpoint; REQ-VET-004 is that requirement (existing behavior, now supported), and REQ-VET-003 is the specialty filter across both forms. REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn; the Superseded entry now points to REQ-VET-004 without reusing the id. PRD: the Known-defect edge case calling the JSON route unsupported is removed. For system-design-expert: system-design.md still says there is no JSON API for the primary workflows, and the Vets/VetController contract rows map to '—' or REQ-VET-001 only; the reinstated surface needs REQ-VET-004 mapping. The vet cache is keyed today on unfiltered queries; how filtered results interact with it is a design matter. The ADR index in docs/adr/README.md is outside my write scope: the new non-goal ADR docs/adr/2026-09-18-non-goal-veterinarian-search-narrowed.md needs an index row (root or system-design-expert). author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Stays inside the vet feature package (system-design § Package Structure). No new module, no service layer, and no cross-package dependency. It follows the paged, declarative repository-query shape of owner search (OwnerRepository#findByLastNameStartingWith; grep-based, IDE oracle not connected). New ground, recorded in docs/adr/2026-09-18-vet-directory-filtering-in-the-database-uncached.md: (1) each directory filter is a parameterized VetRepository query. It pages in the database, matches the whole Specialty name ignoring case, and returns each Vet once. (2) Filtered reads carry NO @Cacheable, because a caller-supplied name would otherwise become a permanent key in the unbounded 'vets' cache. Only the existing unfiltered findAll()/findAll(Pageable) stay cached. (3) VetController binds an optional 'specialty' request parameter on both /vets.html and /vets. Absent or blank (strip().isEmpty()) routes to the existing cached unfiltered read. Any other value is passed to the query unchanged, and no test locks padded or repeated values (PRD Open Questions). /vets stays unpaged and returns the Vets wrapper. (4) vetList.html page links carry the active specialty through Thymeleaf link-expression parameters, e.g. @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}, so the value is URL-encoded. They emit no specialty parameter when none is active. Paging counts come from the filtered Page, so totalPages reflects only the narrowed list. The machine-readable list (REQ-VET-004) is existing behavior, now mapped in Contracts. Its Known Defects row is removed.
integration_points: Repository boundary (matching semantics): tested in ClinicServiceTests against the REAL H2 database and seed data, no double. Cover a case-differing name (e.g. 'SURGERY'), a prefix that must not match ('surg'), an unknown name giving an empty result, Linda Douglas (surgery+dentistry) appearing once with both specialties, and a narrowed page with a small PageRequest (e.g. size 1 on 'surgery': totalElements 2, totalPages 2). The seed narrowed lists never exceed the controller's page size, so multi-page counting is proven here.

Framework transport (VetControllerTests, @WebMvcTest + MockMvc): keep the file's existing @MockitoBean VetRepository stub as the double. Reason: the controller logic under test is blank-to-absent routing, parameter forwarding, the filtered Page reaching the model, and page links carrying the specialty. None of it depends on matching, which the real-database tests prove. A multi-page filtered PageImpl drives the link test. No other new stub.
Binding target, /vets.html: an optional String request parameter 'specialty' plus the existing int 'page'. Both are request-scoped scalars, and no persisted type is bound.
Binding target, /vets: the same optional String request parameter 'specialty', a request-scoped scalar. No persisted type is bound.

Trust boundary: the specialty text is external input (security-principles § Trust Boundaries). It reaches the database only as a bound query parameter (derived query or @Query with a named parameter), and it reaches HTML only through escaped Thymeleaf link-expression parameters.

patterns.description: Paged derived query taking a caller-supplied string plus a Pageable; the shape the specialty query follows (the match is whole-name ignoring case, not prefix)
findPaginated/addPaginationModel helpers: extend them to take the normalized specialty rather than adding a parallel paging path

risks.risk: A join on specialties duplicates a Vet holding several matching rows, or inflates the count query, which breaks edge case 3 and page counts.
risks.mitigation: Use a DISTINCT derived query (e.g. findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase) or an explicit @Query with an EXISTS subquery and a matching countQuery. Prove it on real H2 with Linda Douglas (system-design § Contracts, VetRepository row).

risks.risk: Adding @Cacheable to a filtered read turns caller text into unbounded cache keys (memory growth).
risks.mitigation: Filtered reads carry no cache annotation (docs/adr/2026-09-18-vet-directory-filtering-in-the-database-uncached.md; architecture-principles Design Principle 1, resource limits).

risks.risk: Building page links by string concatenation or __${}__ preprocessing with the specialty value allows markup or URL injection.
risks.mitigation: Use Thymeleaf link-expression parameters only (security-principles § Realization, Cross-site scripting row).

risks.risk: Filtered results render a narrowed Vet with only the matched specialty, if the query fetch-joins the specialties collection.
risks.mitigation: Filter through a non-fetch join or subquery. The EAGER specialties mapping then loads each Vet's full set (edge case 3).

risks.risk: Blank handling or whole-name matching is placed in the controller as a business rule.
risks.mitigation: Blank-to-absent is parameter normalization, which is binding (architecture-principles § pattern catalog, Web controller row). Matching lives in the repository query only.

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records on the log; skipped. Design writes: docs/system-design.md. The Overview names the vet list as the one machine-readable surface. Contracts rows map REQ-VET-003/004 on Vet, Specialty, Vets, VetRepository, VetController and CacheConfiguration. Security Context adds the specialty input and the supported output. The Known Defects row for the unsupported machine-readable route is removed, since the owner reinstated it. New ADR: docs/adr/2026-09-18-vet-directory-filtering-in-the-database-uncached.md. docs/adr/README.md index gains rows for it and for the product expert's non-goal ADR (2026-09-18-non-goal-veterinarian-search-narrowed.md). The existing showResourcesVetList test may be kept or renamed to carry theVetListDocumentShouldReturnEveryVetWithTheirSpecialties. The PRD settles which. The page's existing 'page' parameter as a cache key is pre-existing exposure (Open Question 5) and out of this slice.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: the request-supplied specialty only reaches the Spring Data derived queries findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String) and findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String, Pageable) (VetRepository.java, added in the diff), which bind it as a parameter. No query text is concatenated, and an IgnoreCase equality match has no LIKE wildcard for a caller to abuse.

Cross-site scripting and URL injection in vetList.html: the specialty goes back into the page only as a Thymeleaf link-expression parameter, e.g. @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}, which URL-encodes the value, and th:href escapes the attribute. The change also removes the old __${...}__ preprocessing from the vet pagination links. A grep -F '__${' over src/main/resources/templates finds the remaining uses only in fragments/inputField.html, selectField.html, layout.html and owners/ownerDetails.html, where they carry fragment parameters and entity ids, not request text. These uses predate this change and are unchanged.

Cache exhaustion: the filtered queries are deliberately not @Cacheable, so caller text never becomes a key in the 'vets' cache. A blank specialty falls back to the cached unfiltered findAll (VetController.activeSpecialty filters with Predicate.not(String::isBlank)).

Empty result: a specialty that matches nothing gives totalPages 0, and the pagination block is guarded by th:if="${totalPages > 1}" (vetList.html), so the view renders no link to page 0 and no invalid PageRequest.

The JSON /vets route still serves read-only vet data. The specialty is only a filter and is never echoed back, and the change adds no new endpoint, request-body binding, @ModelAttribute target, logging, or file access.
No secrets are added: the production diff introduces no credential, token, or key literal.

Supply chain: build.gradle, pom.xml and gradle/ are unchanged (git diff --stat is empty). ./gradlew dependencies resolves Spring Boot 4.1.1, tools.jackson.core jackson-databind 3.1.5, Thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE and Hibernate 7.4.5.Final. dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured, so no NVD match ran in this review.

approved_aspects: Fix-delta scope: `python3 scripts/changeset.py --base-tree 4b596a8eac3a4c7060a9c5625e897d457a8dc8bb` shows only src/main/resources/templates/vets/vetList.html changed since my round-1 approval. author: change-grader
summary: filter the vet directory by specialty on both routes

blast_radius.note: Three production files in the vet feature package (controller, repository, one template), no sensitive paths, no dependency or schema change; the doc edits narrow NG-9 and mint REQ-VET-004 as the owner instructed.

semantic_surprise.note: The fix-round refactor of vetList.html puts th:if and th:replace on the same <a> (lines 36, 41, 45, 49, 53). In Thymeleaf 3.1.5, th:replace runs first (StandardReplaceTagProcessor.PRECEDENCE = 100, StandardIfTagProcessor.PRECEDENCE = 300, read from the resolved jar), so the host element and its th:if are replaced before the condition is checked. Every pagination link then renders unconditionally. Page 1 shows First and Previous links, and Previous points at page=0, which PageRequest.of(-1, 5) rejects, so following it shows the error page. The current page number appears both as a link and as plain text, and on the last page Next points past the end. This also hits the unfiltered directory: the seed data has 6 vets and the page size is 5, so there are 2 pages. The requirement says that naming no specialty leaves the directory as it was, and this breaks that. The controller and repository logic reads correctly: blank values fall back to the cached findAll, and the filtered queries are uncached derived queries with DISTINCT.

test_adequacy.note: The repository tests run against real H2 seed data and cover matching by whole name ignoring case, the prefix non-match, the unknown-name empty result, the vet listed once, and filtered page counts. The link tests only check that a page-2 href is present (with or without specialty). Nothing checks that the First and Previous links are absent on page 1 or that the current page is not a link, so the suite stays green against the regressed template.

reviewer_hedging.note: All dispatched reviewers approved, and the fix-round roster of code-quality and security was the plan's expected scope. But the template rewrite landed after test-reviewer's approval. Code-quality's approval says the th:block th:if=false fragment idiom works but gives no rendering evidence. It also cites vetList.html lines 34 and 38, which are span lines, while the call sites are lines 36, 41, 45, 49 and 53. Security's note that dependency checking is not configured is a known project gap, recorded here as context only.

scope_deviation.note: The diff follows the intake decisions: the parameter is set only through the URL with no page control, the specialty is carried in page links, blank counts as absent, REQ-VET-004 is minted and REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn, and the padded-value and repeated-value questions are recorded as open. There were no design revisions, consultations or build retries.

rationale: Behind the correct controller and repository work, the round-2 template refactor likely drops every pagination th:if because th:replace runs before th:if, so page 1 of the unfiltered directory links to page=0 and gets an error page. Render /vets.html page 1 and the last page before merging; the tests would not catch this.
